interface.title: population-pulse
interface.field: Public health surveillance / epidemiology (respiratory emergency-department demand vs. population-mobility, weather and wastewater signals)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory and descriptive analysis: finding lead-lag relationships, then screening regression models and checking them before any causal or event-study follow-up
interface.what_it_is_for: Line up weekly city signals (transit, bikeshare, weather, events, academic calendar, wastewater by pathogen) against respiratory ED demand, find which drivers lead demand and by how many weeks with multiple-comparison correction, then fit and check surge and count regressions for overfitting and confounding.

data.note: Built-in Boston parquet files. The data is partly real and partly synthetic. hospital_demand (MA DPH, 2019-06 onward), events and academic_calendar come from real checked-in CSVs. Transit, bikeshare, weather and wastewater are synthetic samples. 'boston' is the only City option (screens/047.webp). Each signal covers a different span: transit, bikeshare and weather run 2018-07 to 2026-10; hospital_demand 2019-06 to 2026-07; wastewater 2022-12 on; transit_service_level only from 2025-10 (screens/005.webp). The 8 most recent weeks of demand are marked provisional and left out of the correlation and regression.

tree.general: Find which outside signals lead a weekly health outcome, by how much, and whether that lead holds up under multiple-testing correction, out-of-sample validation and a confounding check
tree.specific: Find which Boston drivers (transit, bikeshare, weather, events, academic calendar, wastewater Influenza A/RSV/SARS-CoV-2) lead respiratory ED demand, and test that with BH correction, walk-forward folds and VIF

features.name: Multi-signal z-score timeline with event annotations
features.general: Choose any set of time series, rescale each to z-scores over the selected window, and overlay them on one time axis with hoverable event markers and a provisional-data cutoff line
features.specific: Timeline tab: 'Signals to show' multiselect drives a z-scored Vega line chart with gray dashed event lines (hover shows event, venue, attendance), an orange provisional line, and an 'Aligned weekly data table' expander; follows the sidebar date range
steps: Set the date window (preset or From/To)
Add or remove signals in the multiselect
Compare the overlaid z-scored curves; scroll over the chart to zoom
Hover an event line for details
Expand the aligned weekly table for raw values
serves_tasks: Overlay chosen signals, put on a common scale, against the outcome
Identify marked events on the timeline
Inspect the raw aligned weekly values

features.name: Lagged cross-correlation scan with BH correction and ambiguity flag
features.general: For one predictor, compute correlation with the outcome at each lag in a range, show bars with confidence intervals, name the strongest lag with raw and FDR-corrected p-values, and warn when the top lag's interval overlaps the runner-up's
features.specific: Driver signal selectbox + 'Deseasonalize first' checkbox → lag 0-8 bar chart with CI whiskers, 'Strongest correlation' metric, 'X of 9 lags survive correction (vs. Y before)' text and the 'This lag isn't a clear winner' warning; the best lag is passed on as the default of the regression's Driver lag slider
steps: Choose the driver signal
Optionally turn deseasonalizing off or on
Read the bars and hover for CI bounds, or press Show data for the table
Read the strongest lag with raw vs. BH-corrected p and survival count
Heed or note the ambiguity warning
serves_tasks: Run the lagged correlation for a chosen driver and read the strongest lag
Check whether the best lag survives multiple-comparison correction and whether it clearly beats the next-best lag
Compare results with and without removing the seasonal trend

features.name: Full-scan family-wide significance table
features.general: Correct every predictor × every lag together as one family of tests and list, per predictor, its best lag, effect, raw and corrected p, significance and ambiguity
features.specific: 'Every driver, corrected together (full-scan significance check)' expander: BH correction across 72 driver-lag tests with significant/ambiguous checkboxes per driver
steps: Expand the full-scan section
Sort or scan drivers by corrected p-value
Compare survivors against the count that looked significant before correction
Note which drivers are significant but ambiguous about the lag
serves_tasks: Correct every driver's every lag together, to guard against picking the one driver that happened to survive

features.name: Lagged surge-logistic + count-GLM fit panel
features.general: At a chosen lag, turn the outcome into a binary 'unusually high' label by quantile threshold and fit a logistic model (AUC, pseudo-R², p), and alongside it fit a count GLM with a selectable family (Poisson vs. Negative-Binomial) to compare by AIC
features.specific: Driver lag slider (0-8), Surge threshold (quantile 0.50-0.95) slider and Count regression family selectbox → AUC-ROC, Pseudo-R², driver p-value (surge), plus driver coefficient, p-value and AIC for the GLM. The driver coefficient displays as +0.000 (too few decimals to read)
steps: Accept or move the driver lag
Set the surge quantile threshold
Read AUC, pseudo-R² and p for the surge model
Switch the count family between negative_binomial and poisson
Compare AIC and p-value across families
serves_tasks: Fit a classifier for high-outcome weeks on the lagged driver and read its discrimination
Fit a count model of the outcome and compare distribution families by AIC
Check the automatically chosen lag against a forced nearby lag before trusting either one

features.name: Walk-forward (expanding-window) validation readout
features.general: Refit the current model on past data only across successive time folds and show in-sample vs. out-of-sample metrics with per-fold values, so overfitting shows up as a gap
features.specific: 'Out-of-sample validation (walk-forward)' expander: 5 expanding-window folds with a 52-week minimum training window; AUC-ROC (surge) and mean absolute error, in-sample vs. out-of-sample, per-fold lists; recomputes when the lag, threshold or family changes
steps: Fit a model in the regression panel
Expand the walk-forward section
Compare in-sample and out-of-sample AUC and MAE
Inspect per-fold values for unstable folds
Change lag or family and re-read
serves_tasks: Validate out-of-sample with time-ordered expanding-window folds and compare to the in-sample fit
Check the automatically chosen lag against a forced nearby lag before trusting either one

features.name: Predictor collinearity heatmap + VIF table
features.general: Show a predictor × predictor correlation heatmap (after removing seasonality) with hover values, and a variance-inflation-factor table on the overlapping rows, to flag predictors whose effects could be confounded
features.specific: 'Driver correlation matrix (confounding check)' expander: deseasonalized 8×8 RdBu heatmap with hover tooltip, and a driver/vif/n_obs table with the 'VIF above ~5' guidance
steps: Expand the confounding-check section
Scan the heatmap for strongly coloured off-diagonal cells
Hover a cell to read the pairwise correlation
Read the VIF table and note any driver above ~5
serves_tasks: Check whether drivers are correlated with one another, so an apparent effect isn't carried by a correlated driver
